sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lugos, also written Lugus or Lugoves, was a god of the continental Celts and of Britain. He is the same god who appears in Ireland as Lugh and in Wales as Lleu Llaw Gyffes. In Gaul, people sometimes spoke of a group of three gods called the Lugoves. Some took Lugos for a sun god, but he is better seen as a patron of crafts. The Romans linked him with their own god Mercury, and the link fits because the Celts were famed for their handiwork. His name survives in many place names, such as Lyons and London.

okr.objective: Document Lugos as the continental Celtic god of crafts.
